newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN reports 200 dead in Bangladesh storms.
newsitem.headline: UN reports 200 dead in Bangladesh storms.

text.p: A devastating cyclone in Bangladesh this week killed at least 200 people, the U.N. Department of Humanitarian Affairs (DHA) said on Wednesday.
It also reported widespread destruction of houses after the cyclone roared in from the Bay of Bengal on Monday, battering coastal areas with 200 kph (125 mph) winds and tidal surge.

A DHA statement said the government of the South Asian nation was trying to assess the damage in disaster-hit areas. U.N. relief officials would take part in an airborne survey mission with donor representatives later on Thursday.
Some 1,500 fishermen were missing in the Bay of Bengal, many feared drowned, officials in off-lying islands said.
The DHA said normal communication channels to Cox's Bazar, a port near Bangladesh's border with Burma and one of the areas worst hit by the cyclone, were not functioning.
It reported acute water shortages in the large city of Chittagong because of disruptions in electricity supplies.
Government officials said nearly 400,000 houses had been damaged and more than 1.5 million people left homeless.
Low-lying Bangladesh is prone to ruinous cyclones. A storm in 1991 killed at least 138,000 people and stripped at least one million of shelter.
